meta.title: Squad · manager–worker coordination
meta.subtitle: CLI calls coordinate independent agents through local SQLite state—not a manager daemon.

components.label: Manager agent
components.explanation: The manager role is a prompt, not an autonomous scheduler implemented by Squad. It recommends task create for tracked assignments, send for freeform exchanges, and receive for replies. Inspector review is a prompt-level next step, outside this manager–worker slice.

components.label: squad CLI
components.explanation: A shared implementation invoked separately by each agent. Finds the nearest ancestor workspace containing .squad, opens its messages.db, and checks active agent/session state on task create, ack, complete, send and receive. Join registers the agent, writes a token file, and prints role instructions. Task list and requeue do not take a caller identity. These are local consistency checks, not a manager-only authorization boundary.

components.label: Worker agent
components.explanation: Work execution happens in the external agent, not inside Store. The worker prompt recommends ack then complete for tracked tasks and send for freeform summaries. receive --wait is foreground polling: checks SQLite every 500 ms, refreshes last_seen every 30 s, and exits after a batch or timeout. It takes an exclusive locks/<agent>.receive.lock file so only one waiting receiver per agent runs. A read assignment message is not a task acknowledgement.

components.label: Store · task operations
components.explanation: create requires active creator and assignee and atomically inserts a queued task plus its task_assigned message. ack requires a queued task assigned to the caller, then sets acked, lease_owner and a 15-minute lease timestamp. complete requires acked plus matching lease_owner and writes completed/result_summary; it neither checks lease expiry nor sends a completion message. requeue explicitly resets state and lease fields, optionally replacing the assignee; it does not enqueue a new assignment message. No automatic lease-expiry recovery is established by these operations.

components.label: Store · inbox operations
components.explanation: send inserts a persisted note, optionally carrying task_id and reply_to. Direct send requires an active recipient. receive selects unread messages for the named recipient, orders them by created_at/id, and marks the selected IDs read in the same transaction before the CLI prints them. This is a database mailbox, not a push channel. Consuming a message does not mutate the task status.

components.label: Session token files
components.explanation: Join writes a token to the agent's local file. Session validation compares the local value with the token expected from the agents row; a missing file is allowed for backward compatibility. Waiting receive also captures and rechecks the DB token on every poll. Token checks do not establish OS-level isolation between agents sharing the workspace.

components.label: Shared SQLite database
components.explanation: One local database contains agent identity/activity/session metadata, task assignment/status/lease/result fields, and message envelopes/read flags. Store opens SQLite with WAL journaling and a 5000 ms busy timeout. Despite its filename, messages.db persists both task and message state. Store methods execute SQL directly; there is no separate database service in this path.

boundaries.label: Workspace persistence · shared by CLI invocations

cards.title: Tracked work ≠ message delivery
items: Create: queued task + unread assignment in one transaction.
Ack: queued + assigned caller → acked, with lease owner.
Complete: acked + lease owner → completed + summary.

cards.title: Results need an explicit path
items: Complete does not notify the manager: use task list for state, or send a summary then receive it.
receive --wait polls; it is not a background broker or push subscription.
Requeue is manual; no new assignment message is inserted.

cards.title: Scope and evidence
items: Manager/worker are role prompts, not enforced manager-only permissions.
Overview groups Store methods, not separate processes. Arrows show calls / SQL ownership; output returns through the CLI.
Agent execution and inspector review are outside this slice; crash-durability guarantees are not established here.
